title: Pip Is Never Cold
summary: Pip is the only penguin who never feels cold. He tries everything to cool down, until the iciest night of the winter arrives.

scenes.text:
On an island of ice and snow lived a colony of penguins.

They were all cold. Always. They shivered, they rubbed their flippers, they wore scarves and squashed up close to each other.

All except Pip.

Pip was never cold. While the others shivered, he fanned himself with a flipper.

"Phew, it's so hot!" he'd say, puffing.

His friends would fall about laughing.

"Hot? Here? Pip, we live at the South Pole!"

Pip laughed along with them. But inside, very quietly, he thought: I wish I felt cold too, like everyone else.

One morning, Pip had an idea.

"The sea!" he said. "The sea is freezing!"

He ran to the edge of the ice, took a run-up and dived in head first. Splash!

The water was cold, cold, cold. Pip swam, twirled, blew bubbles. At last he felt nice and cool.

But when he climbed out and shook his feathers, something very strange happened.

Steam came off him. Like a pot of soup.

"Hot again?" sighed Pip, steaming all over.

Pip didn't give up.

He found an enormous block of ice and sat on top of it. He stayed there all morning, very still, waiting to cool down.

But the ice underneath him began to melt. And by midday, Pip was sitting in a puddle.

Then he climbed the highest hill, threw himself down on his tummy and slid all the way to the bottom, with the icy air in his face: whoosh!

"This really works!" he shouted.

Up and down he went, up and down, ten times in a row.

But with all that climbing, when he got to the bottom he was hotter than ever. Red as a tomato and out of breath.

He sat down in the snow, very tired and very thoughtful.

That night came the coldest night of the whole winter. Across the ice, without stopping, blew the wind.

The penguins were shivering so hard that their beaks chattered. The little ones were crying. Nobody could sleep.

And then Pip understood.

He stood in the middle of them all, spread his flippers and said:

"Come here! Come and stand next to me!"

One by one, the penguins came closer. They pressed up against his warm tummy, against his flippers, against his back.

"Pip!" said one of them, surprised. "You're as toasty as a stove!"

That night, no penguin felt cold.

They all stayed squashed together around Pip, in a big ball of feathers, and little by little they stopped shivering. The little ones stopped crying. And one by one, they fell asleep.

Pip looked at them, so calm, so cosy.

And he smiled.

He didn't want to feel cold any more. Now he knew what his warmth was for.

Ever since then, on the iciest nights, all the penguins on the island look for the same thing: a spot next to Pip.
